newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares dragged lower by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares dragged lower by Wall Street.

text.p: German shares took a sharp dive on Monday after Wall Street's tumble on Friday unnerved the market and reignited concerns on U.S. inflation and the risk of higher U.S. interest rates.

The 30-share blue chip DAX index closed the floor session down nearly two percent at 3,279.90 points, although the market pared its losses in the post-bourse session on the firm dollar -- always good news for German exporters.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade, ended the day down 21.72 points at 3,297.52 points, just off a key technical support level at 3,300.
"Maybe the DAX will yet be able to decouple from the U.S.," said one Frankfurt trader of the market's relative resilience.
Very few stocks managed to buck the downward trend, although the dollar-sensitive car sector generally outperformed.
Daimler-Benz ended the post-bourse session up 40 pfennigs at 135.90 marks and BMW rose 7.60 marks to 1,397.70.
Daimler had earlier announced plans to buy into Ballard Power Systems, a Canadian firm that has developed an engine fuelled by hydrogen.
Auto components maker Kolbenschmidt AG firmed 1.20 marks to 29.90 in bourse trade after the Berlin cartel office approved a majority stake in it by the defence and engineering group Rheinmetall.

But the rally that Volkswagen AG has seen after last week's positive 1997 outlook statement was halted, with its shares ending bourse trade off 22.50 marks to 1,050.0 and closing IBIS trade at 1049.80 marks, down 4.20.
Newly-public mobile phone group Mobilcom was sharply lower in bourse trade, down nearly nine percent at 108.50 marks, cutting some of sharp gains since flotation.
